evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2013 (13 years old), 360 m S: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2017 (fire C10784), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
Unnamed wetland 100 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from District of Vanderhoof, about 150 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 53.00864, -124.3881, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 5.8 km S, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 316 m, about 149 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 100 m N of the spot at 1,374 m (52.96095, -124.42086). Water: unnamed wetland 190 m S (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-12, Region 5. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-06, closures 2026-10-16.
R7AA-bear-backcountry-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 5-12: about 412 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.04 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
